newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 392 bln levs May 17.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 392 bln levs May 17.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose some 62 billion levs in the first half of May to 392.3 billion levs, a Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday, quoting preliminary figures.
"The deficit rose to 392.3 billion levs on May 17 mainly due to interest and discount payments on government securities," the official, who declined to be identified told Reuters.
The Finance ministry made a total of 108.3 billion levs interest and discount payments on government securities in the first half of May, Finance ministry figures showed.

The deficit at mid-May was around 1.89 percent of the nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for 1997 assumed in a funding arrangement between the interim government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) sealed in March.
Under the arrangement the budget deficit for this year was assumed at 3.8 percent of projected nominal GDP set at 20.743 trillion levs.
Figures for spending, revenue and deficit as a percentage of budget targets are not available because a viable 1997 budget has yet to be passed by the new parliament.
Under a stop-gap budget bill approved on January 31 the deficit was limited to the volume of interest and discount payments on treasury paper.

The new cabinet which took office last week is in talks with a visiting IMF mission on possible adjustments to GDP and budget deficit projections to take into account changes in the macroeconomic framework since March prior to introduction of a restrictive monetary regime.
The currency board regime would ban central bank refinancing to the Finance ministry and commercial banks.
